nodes.label: Subagents do not commit; the parent commits
nodes.norm_label: subagents do not commit; the parent commits
nodes.summary: Stated as P0-2 and then implemented: a subagent may not commit, branch, push or stash. The parent owns every git operation. Reused id; the rule is stated here in its widest form and the plan template's per-task 'Step 5: Commit' was the conflict it removes.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L9004] Parallel git commits in one repository race on .git/index.lock, so commit ownership moved to the parent and was batched per repo after the diff audit

nodes.label: PR Delivery as the terminal stage of a session
nodes.norm_label: pr delivery as the terminal stage of a session
nodes.summary: A new numbered stage between Step 5 (Verify) and Step 6 (Debt Sweep). Before it, the pipeline's terminal state was a local conventional commit and a clean handoff, so nothing forced a reviewable artifact.

nodes.label: One PR per session, not per subagent
nodes.norm_label: one pr per session, not per subagent
nodes.summary: Granularity was left undefined in the reference material. The decision recorded here: 20 subagents inside one session produce one PR, 20 sessions produce 20 PRs.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L5131] One PR per session because per-chunk granularity multiplies into 200 PRs and kills the merge queue

nodes.label: Branch and worktree names derived by the tool, not chosen by the agent
nodes.norm_label: branch and worktree names derived by the tool, not chosen by the agent
nodes.summary: pr-registry.mjs derives the branch and worktree path and prints the exact git worktree add line. Duplicate branch or worktree is refused at claim, at load and at save, so the uniqueness rule is enforced rather than stated.

nodes.label: Session state machine as a merge gate
nodes.norm_label: session state machine as a merge gate
nodes.summary: isolated -> active -> verified -> open -> merged, with three hard errors: a PR number cannot be recorded before verified (otherwise the sequence skips the evidence gate), only an open session with a PR can merge, and merged is terminal, so a revert is a new session rather than an edit of state.

nodes.label: Topological merge order taken from the plan depends_on DAG
nodes.norm_label: topological merge order taken from the plan depends_on dag
nodes.summary: order is topological over depends_on with a name tiebreak so it is reproducible; surface <s> reports what has to rebase first. Rebase before every merge, resolve inside the session's own branch, verify after every merge.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L5196] Verify after each merge, because 20 merges then one test leaves 19 merges without evidence

nodes.label: A PR is a publication artifact, not a verification executor
nodes.norm_label: a pr is a publication artifact, not a verification executor
nodes.summary: The resolution of the first conflict: the existing rule forbids pushing to make remote runners check, but a PR does trigger them. The precedence written in is that the PR exists for human review and carries the local evidence table, so green local runs stay the gate.

nodes.label: Plan mirrored one-way onto a GitHub issue
nodes.norm_label: plan mirrored one-way onto a github issue
nodes.summary: plan-issue-sync.mjs treats the repository plan as the source and the issue as a derived mirror, giving GitHub-side history of the work alongside the vault mirror. The issue body is the plan text byte for byte plus a plan-sync trailer; a summary body is refused because it becomes a second source of truth that goes stale silently.

nodes.label: Issue number kept in a sidecar, never in plan frontmatter
nodes.norm_label: issue number kept in a sidecar, never in plan frontmatter
nodes.summary: The mapping lives in plan.issues.json. An author-written github_issue frontmatter key is honoured as an override instead of being created over.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L12125] The issue number cannot go in plan frontmatter because the vault publisher hashes the whole plan text, so injecting it would make every mirror stale

nodes.label: Issue body passed on stdin rather than in argv
nodes.norm_label: issue body passed on stdin rather than in argv
nodes.summary: A 10 KB plan in argv hits ARG_MAX and crosses shell quoting rules, so the bytes must land identical to the plan for the mirror premise to hold. A test asserts argv and stdin against the real gh binary on disk.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L12127] The body goes on stdin because byte identity between issue and plan is the only premise the mirror rests on

nodes.label: Issue state derived from the plan status field
nodes.norm_label: issue state derived from the plan status field
nodes.summary: deriveAction is a pure function of (entry, planText, status) returning create, update-body, update-state, update-and-state or current, where current means zero gh calls. Blocked stays open because the work is unfinished; only Complete closes.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L12129] An issue closed by hand does not win, because the issue is derived state and the next sync reopens it

nodes.label: gh issue create and edit have no --json flag
nodes.norm_label: gh issue create and edit have no --json flag
nodes.summary: The first draft added --json to create and edit and passed every stubbed test; only the end-to-end test against the real binary failed. gh issue view is the read path that takes --json, and create/edit return a URL on stdout.

nodes.label: Parent owns the todo list because the subagent has no todo tool
nodes.norm_label: parent owns the todo list because the subagent has no todo tool
nodes.summary: Verified from opencode.ai/docs rather than memory: OpenCode's general subagent has full tool access except todo. So the list is per session, held by the parent, and telling a subagent to make one produces a fake list in its report. todowrite / TodoWrite / update_plan are discovered in the tool catalog, never guessed, and the Plan agent only restricts file edits and bash so planning sessions get one too.

nodes.label: The plan file checklist outranks the tool list when they disagree
nodes.norm_label: the plan file checklist outranks the tool list when they disagree
nodes.summary: Both artifacts are mandatory and neither replaces the other: the tool list is live progress that dies at compaction, the file checklist is the version-controlled record that survives it. On mismatch the file wins and the tool list is corrected.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L12156] Do not skip the list because the widget is missing; the list is the contract and the tool is only how it is displayed

nodes.label: The shipped CLI rejects the database its own sibling app creates
nodes.norm_label: the shipped cli rejects the database its own sibling app creates
nodes.summary: Snipset 0.6.854's schema_migrations.rs adds groups.research_tag; GROUP_COLUMNS in crates/snipset-cli/src/db/fingerprint.rs was not taught the column, so every write is refused with schema_match: false. Root cause is an upstream release defect, not drift on the machine: all seven local binaries were tested and all are 0.2.0 with research_tag appearing zero times.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L18591] research_tag is listed even though the CLI never reads it, because the constant is a fingerprint of the shape the app produces and fail-closed must survive

nodes.label: Fingerprint name-versus-shape agreement
nodes.norm_label: fingerprint name-versus-shape agreement
nodes.summary: Reused id. Here the finding is that GROUP_COLUMNS does double duty: it is the fingerprint expectation and it builds the CREATE TABLE in snipset init, so init and the check agree by construction. A positive control (snipset init then doctor) returned schema_match: true, which refuted the self-inconsistency hypothesis: the CLI is internally consistent but externally stale.

nodes.label: The guard test reads the app's migration source instead of restating the column list
nodes.norm_label: the guard test reads the app's migration source instead of restating the column list
nodes.summary: fingerprint_test.rs parses schema_migrations.rs and checks the relationship between the two lists. The stated reason is that a test rewriting the column list carries the same blind spot and would pass forever.

nodes.label: Migration array position is not cid position
nodes.norm_label: migration array position is not cid position
nodes.summary: An assertion was written and then dropped because the live database disproved it: is_favorite sits at index 9 of the snippet_cols migration array and at cid 9 in the database because it was already in CREATE TABLE, so the has_col check skipped it. SNIPPET_COLUMNS was in fact already correct in true cid order; the replacement assertion claims only what can be proved.

nodes.label: present_triggers only queries the FTS_TRIGGERS subset
nodes.norm_label: present_triggers only queries the fts_triggers subset
nodes.summary: The comparison uses WHERE name IN (FTS_TRIGGERS), so the three embed_snippet_* triggers in the live database are never looked at and the extra triggers a side-by-side diff showed were a false positive of the diff, not drift. Reading the code instead of trusting the diff is what caught it.

nodes.label: schema cli fingerprint guard workflow
nodes.norm_label: schema cli fingerprint guard workflow
nodes.summary: Reused id. The decisive measurement: no workflow in the Snipset repository runs on pull_request and ci.yml is workflow_dispatch only, so a correct guard test does not fire on the pull request that adds a schema migration, which is exactly the moment it must. The written but uncommitted remedy is a path-filtered workflow on schema_migrations.rs and fingerprint.rs.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L19148] A path-filtered trigger is needed because dispatch-only CI never runs on the pull request that adds the migration

nodes.label: A hand-built CLI breaks the runbook byte-identity invariant until a release ships
nodes.norm_label: a hand-built cli breaks the runbook byte-identity invariant until a release ships
nodes.summary: The installed CLI is sha b6aa82ef from a hand build, not the release's 770f29da, so the runbook requirement that ~/.local/bin/snipset be identical to the release sidecar is violated until 0.6.855 ships. Recorded in Snipset PR #440 rather than left as a local binary.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L19200] Keep the hand-built CLI, because reverting to the release binary immediately re-breaks snippet writes

nodes.label: A backup filename's sha was misread as version drift
nodes.norm_label: a backup filename's sha was misread as version drift
nodes.summary: The backup named snipset.bak-770f29da0d03 looked like a stale CLI, but 770f29da is exactly the sha the runbook requires to be installed. Four binaries compared byte-identical to release 0.6.854, so the install was a no-op and the earlier 'CLI stuck at 0.6.852' hypothesis was withdrawn in the answer.

nodes.label: A quiet scp truncated the transfer and still exited 0
nodes.norm_label: a quiet scp truncated the transfer and still exited 0
nodes.summary: 1.7 MB arrived locally against 8.6 MB on the VPS. scp -q printed nothing and was believed on its exit status; the new binary segfaulted with exit 139 and contained none of the expected strings, which is how the truncation was found. Retransfer is verified by hash before the binary is used.

nodes.label: The pgrep bracket trick matched the agent's own compound command line
nodes.norm_label: the pgrep bracket trick matched the agent's own compound command line
nodes.summary: The runbook's pgrep -af "[s]nipset-desktop" preflight exists to avoid matching pgrep itself, but the same compound shell line also contained the literal string in a sha256sum argument, so the check reported the app as running when it was not. Resolved by re-running pgrep standalone.

nodes.label: gh 2.102.0 removed gh issue edit --state
nodes.norm_label: gh 2.102.0 removed gh issue edit --state
nodes.summary: plan-issue-sync.mjs used --state, so every close and reopen would have failed with unknown flag against the installed gh. The class of mistake is identical to the --json assumption caught earlier in the same file, where one instance was fixed and the second left behind.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L20159] The concurrent session's bug report was verified against the installed gh before being accepted

nodes.label: A concurrent session committed onto this session's branch and moved HEAD
nodes.norm_label: a concurrent session committed onto this session's branch and moved head
nodes.summary: Three commits by the same git identity landed at 18:25, 18:27 and 18:31 on the branch that PR #440 was merged from, and a fourth dirty file appeared, which broke this session's commit with cannot lock ref 'HEAD'. Two live opencode processes confirmed a second writer. The same session was found active in ai-skills and on the build host, and its commit fixed a real bug in code already merged to main.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L19847] Unstage the file rather than leave it staged, because loud failure beats silent contamination

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L07612] Stop all work in that repository while another writer is active

nodes.label: Negative control on the fingerprint guard: removing the column fails two tests
nodes.norm_label: negative control on the fingerprint guard: removing the column fails two tests
nodes.summary: Six of six green, then research_tag was temporarily removed and two tests failed with the exact diagnosis, so the guard is real rather than decorative.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - evaluasi-improvement-ai-skills-dari-data [ses_f0a32890affewqrQwI030ukAbI].md:L17370] A guard only ever observed passing is indistinguishable from one that does nothing
